anti_generic_signature_read: The seven-segment numeral on the plinth wall, plus relief coastlines that cast their own shadows onto the ocean and show a real cut wall at the limb.
blind_action_read: None. Static, no mechanism, no pin, no gimbal. The globe is fused to the plate through the collar.
blind_form_read: A full ball on a low cylinder. The cylinder is a clean puck with a softly rounded top edge and a straight vertical side wall, roughly four to five times wider than thick. The ball is about two-thirds the puck's diameter, centred, and meets the plate through a short collar that spreads outward as it descends. The silhouette above that collar is a clean circular arc all the way round. Wider than tall overall, about 1.3 to 1.
blind_held_read: A small model Earth seated on a round flat plinth - a numbered game piece or desk globe, plum-sized on a coaster, one solid unit.
blind_relationship_read: One vertical axis - plate, collar, globe - with a raised numeral on the plinth's side wall directly below the globe's front face. The top view shows the globe inscribed concentrically in the disc.
blind_subjects_read: Earth. Africa with a tan Sahara centre-right, South America tapering to its left, North America upper left, Europe and Asia upper right, the Arabian peninsula as its own tan wedge, the two Americas joined by the Central American isthmus, and a white polar cap on top - from above an irregular ragged white mass ringed by green.

critical_form_requirements.blind_evidence: Blind, before the Wish was shown: 'a small model Earth seated on a round flat plinth'. Briefed: 'blue-ocean, green-continent sphere on a low blue cylinder with a flat top face and a straight vertical wall; the top view confirms a true circular base'.
critical_form_requirements.requirement: A stylized Earth sphere on a flat cylindrical disc base

critical_form_requirements.blind_evidence: Blind: 'the ball is about two-thirds the puck's diameter, centred'. The top view was read as 'the globe inscribed concentrically in the disc with an even blue margin all round'.
critical_form_requirements.requirement: Base 34.0 mm diameter under a 21.08 mm sphere - the sphere reads as roughly 0.62 of the base across

critical_form_requirements.blind_evidence: Blind: 'a clean puck with a softly rounded top edge and a straight vertical side wall, roughly four to five times wider than thick', and 'a straight slab with a flat bottom edge, so it sits flush on a table - no feet, no dish, no taper'.
critical_form_requirements.requirement: Base 5.0 mm tall - a flat disc, not a plinth or a pedestal

critical_form_requirements.blind_evidence: Round four, after the round-three claim of a truncated ball was put back to the critic: 'the silhouette no longer pinches: the profile runs as a continuous circular arc down to where the collar takes over' and the critic explicitly retracted its earlier reading, 'nothing in these images contradicts that'.
critical_form_requirements.requirement: Sphere 21.08 mm diameter, a full sphere rather than a cut or waisted ball

critical_form_requirements.blind_evidence: Briefed, from three independent tells the critic named itself: 'cast shadows from the relief onto the ocean along Africa's north and west coasts', 'the relief's cut side wall visible edge-on at the limb', and 'a visible step of green standing above blue around the cap'. It also judged the depth: 'shallow relative to the ball - consistent with a thin 1 mm skin on a ~21 mm sphere, not a thick shell'.
critical_form_requirements.requirement: Continents raised 1.0 mm in low relief, not printed flat

critical_form_requirements.blind_evidence: Unprompted, the critic named Africa, South America, North America, Europe, Asia, the Arabian peninsula and the polar ice, and settled the abstract-patch question on 'the Central American isthmus - a narrow green thread correctly joining the two American masses'.
critical_form_requirements.requirement: The subjects are Earth's continents, nameable rather than abstract patches

critical_form_requirements.blind_evidence: 'Four discrete straight bars with gaps between them: a short vertical at upper left, a short vertical at upper right, a horizontal crossbar joining their lower ends, and a vertical dropping below the crossbar on the right. No closed loop, no curve, no diagonal.' The critic read it as a 4 at a glance.
critical_form_requirements.requirement: Rank numeral 4 built from seven-segment bars, not a drawn digit

critical_form_requirements.blind_evidence: 'The numeral is on the vertical side wall at the globe's centre line, at reading height across a board', and blind, before the brief, it was placed 'on the plinth rim, centred under Africa'.
critical_form_requirements.requirement: The numeral sits on the disc side wall where a seated player reads it, not on the globe

critical_form_requirements.blind_evidence: 'Six views, no axis rod, no gimbal, no pivot, no parting line', and on the explicit negative list: 'None of the listed items is present ... the plinth is uniformly blue in all six views'. The one item the critic first called unaccounted for, a tab on the plate rim, it withdrew on inspection as the numeral seen end-on from above.
critical_form_requirements.requirement: Negative: a static game piece with no mechanism - no stand beyond the disc, no spindle, no axis pin, no hollow, no hole, no text, no logo, no second base colour

largest_risk: Nothing here has been printed. The relief is 1.0 mm of ground on a 21.08 mm ball, and every south-facing coastline ramps down to a feather edge at its toe; check_thickness at a 0.4 mm nozzle classes 47 such regions as tapers inside its 2 percent budget rather than as thin walls, and check_overhang finds no region needing support, but neither gate says whether those edges survive being tipped into a bag with the rest of the set. The critic raised the same worry from the images in round three and it drove the repair that stopped north-facing walls leaning, which is what had been producing genuine undercut lips; what remains is a bevel that runs out to nothing, not a lip. It is still the first thing that would chip.
resolution: Four review rounds, the allowance in full. Round one was fully blind and failed: the relief read as floating shards, the globe/disc seam as a torn fringe, the base as two materials. That last was self-inflicted - the canonical images came from render_product, which is two-tone by face orientation and ignores the colours sealed on the occurrences - so the family was rebuilt with render_review, which keeps them. Round two cleared that and isolated one blocker: white ice at the foot of the globe faces downward, shades to grey, and read as bare unpainted material. The ice was removed and the seat finished in the ocean's own blue. Round three, with the Wish revealed, matched every positive and negative held-form requirement and called the piece desirable, naming four faults. Three were repaired: walls facing north no longer borrow a lean from their neighbours, which had been producing undercut lips; the seat now spreads outward to the disc face instead of tucking in; the polar rim is broken by six lobes rather than an exact circle of latitude. Round four withdrew two of its own findings once told that the top-view nub is the numeral seen end-on and that the seat is material added around a full 21.08 mm sphere, confirmed the waist resolved, matched all eight brief checks and returned desirable. It left one conditional blocker: a quilted shading patch on the ocean east of Africa, to be cleared by a mesh check for coincident or self-intersecting surfaces. That check is clean - inspect validate ok with no findings on both entries, inspect interfere 0 clashes, check_mesh printable with 0 boundary edges, 0 non-manifold edges, 0 pinched vertices, consistent winding, positive volume, one shell. On the critic's own condition that makes it a shading artefact, not a blocker. Motion is unverified: check_motion is false for this run and the piece has no mechanism.
reviewer: independent native critic agent, given the render family and nothing else; four rounds, the Wish withheld until round three
